title: Seawall Rules in Broward County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Broward County?
qualifier: Broward is the one county in South Florida with a single standard behind every city. The county set it, and every municipality had to adopt it locally by February 2022. That makes the county rule the floor everywhere — but several cities went further, so the number that applies to you is your city's, not the county's.
detail_rows: The county floor :: 4 ft NAVD88 for a barrier built before 1 January 2035, rising to 5 ft NAVD88 by 2050. | Where it comes from :: Broward County Code Chapter 39, Article XXV, Resiliency Standards for Tidal Flood Protection. | Who it applies to :: New tidal flood barriers, and existing ones substantially improved by more than 50% in length or cost. | Why your city may be higher :: The county set a minimum. Cities were free to adopt something stricter, and some did. | Fort Lauderdale :: 5.0 ft NAVD88. An application before 1 January 2035 may build to 4.0 ft if designed to reach 5.0 ft by 2050. | Pompano Beach :: 5 ft NAVD88 minimum and 5 ft 10 in maximum. The only city in the county that caps the height as well as setting a floor. | Hollywood :: 4 ft NAVD88 until 2035, then 5 ft. The county standard, adopted as written. | The practical point :: Build to 4 ft today and the wall has to come up again before 2050. Ask what it costs to build for 5 ft now, while the barge is already there.
source: Broward County Code Ch. 39, Art. XXV, Resiliency Standards for Tidal Flood Protection

title: Seawall Rules in Miami-Dade County
question: What are the seawall requirements in Miami-Dade County?
unit: the number is set by your city
qualifier: Miami-Dade works the opposite way to Broward. The county runs the environmental permit through Chapter 24, but it sets no countywide seawall elevation — that is your city's decision, and the cities differ sharply. What the county does control is how far waterward you may rebuild, and that single measurement decides whether your permit takes weeks or months.
detail_rows: The county's part :: Chapter 24 environmental permitting through DERM, which applies inside every city in the county. | The 18-inch rule :: A seawall rebuilt up to 18 inches waterward of its existing line qualifies for an administrative short-form permit. Beyond that it goes to a public hearing before the Board of County Commissioners. | Why that matters :: It is the difference between a permit measured in weeks and one measured in months. The threshold was raised from 12 inches in 2024, so older guidance is out of date. | Where it is written :: Miami-Dade County Code Section 24-48.2. | Elevation is municipal :: The county sets no height. Miami Beach requires 5.7 ft NAVD88. Other cities set their own, and several have not published one at all. | Miami Beach specifically :: 5.7 ft NAVD88 for new or substantially improved walls, with an interim 4.0 ft allowed for lesser repairs if the wall is built to accept 5.7 ft later. Substantial now means repairs of $500 or more per linear foot, raised from $300 in July 2025. | Budget for a bond :: Some cities in the county require a refundable bond on top of the contract. Coral Gables has asked for $15,000. Ask before you sign.
source: Miami-Dade County Code Sec. 24-48.2 (as amended 2024); City of Miami Beach Code Sec. 54-62(a), Ordinance 2025-4754
